subject: Physical sealing, runtime logs, and retention posture for Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Alice Wang <alice.wang@continentalbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Dedicated deployment - physical sealing + logs retention questions

Jordan,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of Continental Bank's procurement checklist we need written confirmation of a few items for the Dedicated cluster you plan to provision for us:

1) "Physical sealing" / non-replication assurances — can you describe what you mean operationally? Are snapshots or backups ever replicated outside the pinned region?
2) Runtime logs — which categories of logs are retained outside the tenant boundary (request traces, host metrics, kernel-level logs)? We need a retention matrix per log type.
3) Evidence for wipe — when a tenant is decommissioned, what artifacts will you provide as proof that data was erased? We need an example certificate or template.

Please respond with a short runbook and any sample artifacts. Also include expected SLAs/timelines for a tenant purge request.

Regards,
Alice Wang
SecOps Lead, Continental Bank
security@continentalbank.com
(attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Wang <alice.wang@continentalbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 13:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment - physical sealing + logs retention questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I've looped in Karthik (product infra) and Ben (ops) to provide the runbook and sample certs. Short version:

- Physical sealing / replication: Dedicated clusters can be anchored to a single region and we do not replicate tenant data to other regions unless explicitly configured for multi-region DR. Snapshots are taken as point-in-time encrypted artifacts and, for region-anchored deployments, those snapshots are stored in region-local object stores by default.

- Runtime logs: We separate logs into three buckets:
  * Tenant-scoped request traces (saved only in tenant storage or tenant-scoped logging stream)
  * Host/infra metrics (aggregated, anonymized; stored in monitoring cluster but not tied to tenant data)
  * System/kernel logs (retention depends on host OS policies; we provide filtered extracts for audits)

- Wipe proof: We provide a signed erase attestation that includes wipe timestamps, snapshot hashes (where applicable), and the operator runbook used. Example certificate attached (tenant-erase-cert-sample.pem).

Action items for your procurement doc:
 1) Ben will send the site-seal checklist (ops steps + controls) and a sample log-retention-matrix.
 2) Karthik will add the pinning/replication clause language for the contract.

Ben / Karthik — can you attach the two artifacts and confirm the expected purge timeline (standard / accelerated)?

Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
(attachment: none)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment - physical sealing + logs retention questions

Jordan / Karthik — attaching two artifacts for Continental Bank: site-seal-checklist.pdf and log-retention-matrix.csv. Key points from ops team:

- Site seal checklist (attachment) summarizes the steps we perform during provisioning to bind a tenant to a region:
  1) Provision tenant-scoped VPC and storage with region constraints.
  2) Disable cross-region replication flags for tenant buckets.
  3) Mark infra images/snapshots with tenant and region metadata and restrict cross-region snapshot exports.
  4) Store snapshots encrypted with a region-scoped KMS key (customer-managed when requested).

- Purge timelines:
  * Standard purge (policy-driven): 30–45 calendar days to complete internal wipe + verification (includes snapshot tombstoning and background zeroing).
  * Expedited purge (legal/urgent): 5–7 calendar days with SOC oversight; we generate a signed erase attestation and provide hash digests for verification.

- Log handling specifics (see CSV):
  * Request traces: tenant-scoped, retention default 90 days (configurable). Export to external SIEM only with customer opt-in.
  * Host metrics: aggregated; retained 365 days for performance analytics, no tenant identifiers.
  * System logs: retained 30 days by default; for audits we extract correlated slices and redact host IDs.

I'll follow up with the sample erase certificate after a quick redaction pass.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: site-seal-checklist.pdf; log-retention-matrix.csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Wang <alice.wang@continentalbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 16:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment - physical sealing + logs retention questions

Alice — following up with the contractual language and an example erase attestation. We avoid the term 'sealed' in contract text and instead specify the operational controls that enforce locality:

Proposed clause (draft):
"Tenant data for Dedicated deployment will be stored and processed solely within the designated region(s) as specified in the order form. Redwood Inference will not replicate tenant data to other regions except for customer-authorized disaster recovery configurations or where required by law. Snapshots and backups created for the tenant will be encrypted at rest using region-scoped keys and retained according to the retention schedule in Appendix A. Upon decommissioning, Redwood will execute the tenant erase workflow and provide a signed erase attestation documenting the wipe activities and artifacts."

Attached: tenant-erase-cert-sample.pem (PEM-format sample of what we provide after a purge). Note: the certificate includes: tenant id, wipe timestamps, list of erased object hashes, operator id, and signature chain anchored to our compliance signing key.

If Continental Bank would prefer a customer-managed KMS for final encryption (so snapshots can only be unsealed with their key), we can enable that during provisioning — please confirm.

Next steps: Jordan to coordinate scheduling of a short technical demo of the purge runbook for your auditors (30 minutes). Ben to confirm we can meet the expedited 5–7 day SLA on request.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
(attachment: tenant-erase-cert-sample.pem)
